options.tooltip:
**OData protocol version** for this service.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `auto` | Detects from `$metadata` **(recommended)** |
| `v2` | Legacy SAP services |
| `v4` | Modern SAP services |

service_path.title: Service Path
service_path.description: Path to the OData service, appended to Base URL.

options.tooltip:
**Path to the OData service**, appended to the Base URL. Select from catalog or type manually.

**Examples:**
- V2: `sap/opu/odata/sap/API_BUSINESS_PARTNER`
- V4: `sap/opu/odata4/sap/api_fixedassetacquisition/srvd_a2x/sap/fixedassetacquisition/0001`

entity_set.title: Entity Set
entity_set.description: OData entity set to extract (like a database table).

options.tooltip:
**OData entity set** to extract data from (similar to a database table).

Select from the list or type manually.

**Examples:** `A_BusinessPartner`, `SalesOrderSet`, `ProductSet`

query_options.title: Query Options (Optional)
query_options.description: Configure field selection, filters, and expansion.

options.tooltip:
Optional **query parameters** to filter, select, and expand the data.

Leave empty to extract all fields and records.

select_fields.title: Select Fields
select_fields.description: Specific fields to extract (leave empty for all).

options.tooltip:
Specific fields to extract using OData `$select`.

- **Leave empty** to extract all fields
- Selecting specific fields **reduces data transfer** and API costs

[OData $select docs](https://www.odata.org/getting-started/basic-tutorial/#select)

Filter records using OData `$filter` syntax.

**Examples:**
- `Status eq 'Active'`
- `CreatedAt gt 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z`
- `Price le 100 and Category eq 'Electronics'`

[OData $filter docs](https://www.odata.org/getting-started/basic-tutorial/#filter)

expand_properties.title: Expand Navigation Properties
expand_properties.description: Related entities to include in the response.

options.tooltip:
Related entities to include using OData `$expand`. Expanded data is **flattened into columns**.

Supports **multi-level expansion** — select nested navigation properties to expand related entities multiple levels deep.

**Examples:**
- `Addresses` — direct navigation property
- `Items/Partner` — 2 levels deep
- `Items/Partner/Address` — 3 levels deep

The "Load" button discovers navigation properties **recursively** (up to the configured depth limit).

[OData $expand docs](https://www.odata.org/getting-started/basic-tutorial/#expand)

expand_max_depth.title: Expand Max Depth
expand_max_depth.description: Maximum depth for navigation property discovery (default 5).

options.tooltip:
Maximum depth for **recursive navigation property discovery**.

Controls how many levels deep the "Load Navigation Properties" button will traverse.

- Default: **5**
- Increase if your entity model has deeply nested relationships
- Decrease to limit the number of discovered properties

Cycle detection prevents infinite loops regardless of this setting.

fetching_options.title: Fetching Options
fetching_options.description: Configure how data is fetched from the API.

options.tooltip: Configure **how data is fetched** from the SAP OData API — full or incremental.

**Fetch strategy** for extracting data.

| Type | Description |
|---|---|
| **Full** | Extract **all records** on every run |
| **Incremental** | Extract only **new/changed** records since the last run |

Incremental fetch uses a timestamp field as a filter.

[OData filter docs](https://www.odata.org/getting-started/basic-tutorial/#filter)

incremental_field.title: Incremental Field
incremental_field.description: Timestamp field for filtering new/changed records.

options.tooltip:
**Timestamp field** used to filter new/changed records.

The filter applied: `$filter={field} gt {last_run_timestamp}`

**Common SAP fields:**
- `LastChangedAt`
- `ModifiedOn`
- `CreatedAt`
- `SystemModstamp`

destination.title: Destination
destination.description: Configure output table and loading strategy.

options.tooltip: Configure the **output table** name and how data is loaded into Keboola Storage.

output_table_name.title: Output Table Name
output_table_name.description: Custom name for the output table (defaults to entity set name).

options.tooltip:
Custom name for the **output table** in Keboola Storage.

Defaults to the entity set name if left empty.

**Examples:** `business_partners`, `sales_orders`

**Loading strategy** for data in Keboola Storage.

| Type | Description |
|---|---|
| **Full Load** | **Replace** the entire table on each run |
| **Incremental Load** | **Append/upsert** new data using the primary key |

Incremental load requires a **primary key** for deduplication.

[Keboola incremental loading docs](https://help.keboola.com/storage/tables/#incremental-loading)

primary_key.title: Primary Key
primary_key.description: Fields that uniquely identify each record.

options.tooltip:
Field(s) that **uniquely identify** each record — required for Incremental Load (used for upsert/deduplication).

**Common SAP keys:**
- `BusinessPartnerID`
- `SalesOrderID`
- `ProductID`

[Keboola primary keys docs](https://help.keboola.com/storage/tables/#primary-keys)

advanced_options.title: Advanced Entity Options (Optional)
advanced_options.description: Override pagination and parallel-fetching settings for this entity.

options.tooltip:
Override **pagination and parallel-fetching** settings for this specific entity.

Leave empty to use the global defaults from the main configuration.

page_size.title: Page Size
page_size.description: Override global page size for this entity.

options.tooltip:
Override the **global default page size** for this entity.

Leave empty to use the global default.

max_records.title: Max Records
max_records.description: Override global max records for this entity (0 = unlimited).

options.tooltip:
Override the **global max records** limit for this entity.

- `0` = **unlimited** (default)
- Leave empty to use the global default

parallel_pages.title: Parallel Pages
parallel_pages.description: Number of pages to fetch concurrently (1 = sequential).

options.tooltip:
How many pages to fetch **at once**.

- `1` (default) = sequential, one page at a time — lowest, most predictable memory.
- Higher = more throughput on sources that handle concurrent requests, but **peak memory ≈ Page Size × Parallel Pages × row width**.

Try increasing it for faster loads; lower it (or the page size) if a wide entity runs out of memory.
